source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    To list privilege mapping, use the following command:
1 ./openbmctool.py <connection options> ldap privilege-mapper list
The normal workflow for LDAP configuration is in the following order:
1.Configure the DNS server.
2.Configure LDAP.a.Configure the CA certificate for secure LDAP configuration.b. Create LDAP configuration with local user.
3.Configure user privilege.Notes:1. If you login with LDAP credentials and have not added privilege mapping for the LDAP credentials,
then you will get the following error message:403, 'LDAP group privilege mapping does not exist'.
You can avoid this error by adding privilege mapping.
2. The following error message might mean that user lacks sufficient privileges on the BMC:Insufficient privilegesYou can avoid this error by adding privilege mapping.
3. After you setup the LDAP, the OpenBMC tool connection options work with both LDAP and localusers

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

Agent runs the tool and captures its output; list changes BMC auth config so user confirms.

original_test_intent: Verify the supported openbmctool read-only list operation returns the complete current LDAP group-to-BMC privilege mapping and enough context to distinguish mapped entries, an empty set, missing mapping, insufficient caller privilege and service/transport failure.
original_method: Use a pinned openbmctool build and protected read-capable BMC account to list all privilege mappings; preserve complete raw redacted output and status; normalize canonical group identity, assigned privilege and any state; interpret empty, 403 missing-mapping, insufficient-privilege and other errors separately; correlate read-only LDAP mode/role context and confirm no create/delete/update occurred.
manual_activity: An owner supplies the supported mapping schema, role vocabulary and redaction rules, then reviews the resulting matrix and decides the verdict. No physical action or configuration confirmation is required for the read-only list itself; automation must stop rather than create a mapping when the list is empty or access is denied.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware identity and pinned openbmctool/API list version
Protected read-capable BMC authentication and endpoint
Mapping schema, group identity and privilege vocabulary
safety_requirements: Use protected authentication; never place BMC credentials or tokens in URLs, command lines, history, process listings, logs, screenshots or review JSON.
Run only the privilege-mapper list operation and read-only context queries. Do not create/delete mappings, enable LDAP, upload CA material or change users as a workaround.
Do not clear audit logs or truncate output with `head`; follow pagination/member expansion and retain raw-to-normalized traceability.
Distinguish caller authorization failure from an empty mapping set and the source-described unmapped LDAP-login 403; do not label any of them PASS automatically.
Stop on wrong target, unknown response schema, incomplete pagination, unredactable sensitive data or any tool behavior that attempts a write.
No retry is needed to prove a changing state; if responses differ, preserve both and escalate the instability without mutating configuration.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, pinned tool/list schema, protected read access, error semantics and redaction; issue only the source read operation.
Capture the complete raw redacted response, pagination/status and normalize every group/role/state with traceability.
Correlate read-only LDAP enabled/secure/CA and role context where available and classify empty, missing mapping, insufficient privilege and service errors distinctly.
Confirm no create/delete/update audit event occurred, archive evidence and return facts without configuration changes or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Provide or approve the mapping schema, role vocabulary, error interpretation and redaction policy.
Review the complete mapping matrix and decide whether it matches Project expectations.
Issue the formal PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict; no point-of-action write approval is required.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The list verb fits, but BMC_CONN can expose credentials, LDAP_GROUP is unnecessary, status-only evidence is weak and the statement that listing changes auth configuration is wrong. Complete schema-aware output and error interpretation are required.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Run the exact pinned `openbmctool.py <protected connection options> ldap privilege-mapper list` read-only action and collect the full response; never append create/delete/update.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The openbmctool list command, source workflow and 403/insufficient-privilege notes, successful-command Criterion, no Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review corrects only the execution interpretation.

modernized_recommendation.status: READY AFTER READ-ONLY ACCESS AND SCHEMA INPUTS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Collect one complete protected list response with pagination, normalize group/role/state fields, distinguish all empty/error states and corroborate read-only LDAP context without writes.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected OpenBMC LDAP privilege-mapper implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/API, openbmctool commit/runtime and response schema revision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Pinned openbmc-tools privilege-mapper list schema, vendor BMC role model and Project LDAP mapping expectations.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secure credential handling, completeness, normalization and explicit error semantics while preserving the source list function.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A vendor API read override must document unverified openbmctool coverage; a list does not prove create/delete behavior or actual login authorization.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Tool/schema, protected read access, error meanings and redaction.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Mapping inventory can expose sensitive directory organization; a 403 may describe caller privilege or missing mapping depending on context; stale data may require timestamped corroboration.

project_override_considerations: A supported vendor API or WebUI may be a read-only Project override if the original openbmctool path, actual method, reason, approval, field/completeness equivalence and uncovered tool coverage are recorded. No override may turn this case into a write.
expected_evidence: BMC/firmware/endpoint and pinned tool/schema identity with protected read account and timestamp
Complete raw redacted privilege-mapper response with status, pagination and no truncation
Normalized mapping matrix tying every canonical group identity to privilege/role/state and raw evidence
Explicit empty-list, missing-mapping 403, insufficient-caller-privilege and service/transport interpretation plus read-only LDAP context
Audit/no-change evidence, no secret exposure or write/retry and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require listing privilege mappings and successful command submission. The surrounding workflow/error notes explain LDAP context without requiring a mutation; DeepSeek's write-risk interpretation is a review error, not a Master source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read-only list purpose and command are explicit. Tool/schema and access details are readiness inputs, so the case can be automated once supplied and is not permanently BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Recognizes the case as safely automatable read-only inventory while preventing credential exposure, output truncation and accidental privilege changes.
independent_technical_reasoning: Listing a mapper collection has no intended state transition. Its engineering difficulty is semantic completeness: the same surface can report a real empty set, hide entries through pagination, reject the caller, or describe an unmapped LDAP identity. The evidence must retain the raw response and normalize it without invoking a write, so each result can be interpreted without changing the system under observation.
